subject.title: Add loop-aware compaction guard for saturated sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a new saturated-session compaction guard surface beyond tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard and compaction qualityGuard, and what config/default/reset policy should it use?
rationale: The remaining work adds public config/default semantics and decides when OpenClaw should strengthen compaction, validate summaries, and recommend reset after degraded session state; source inspection cannot choose that product contract safely.

options.title: Keep As Maintainer Design Work
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the config namespace, default behavior, validator contract, and reset-recommendation policy before accepting or replacing the config-scaffold PR.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Follow-Ups
options.body: Move implementation pieces into separate issues for tail classification, guarded summary quality, post-compaction loop handling, and compaction rate limiting, then close this umbrella only after ownership is clear.

options.title: Decline New Guard Surface
options.body: Rely on the shipped safeguard quality guard and post-compaction identical-tool abort, and close the separate compaction.guard config direction as too much new core surface.

recommendation.title: Keep As Maintainer Design Work
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the config namespace, default behavior, validator contract, and reset-recommendation policy before accepting or replacing the config-scaffold PR.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across compaction safeguard schema, quality helpers, and post-compaction guard policy surfaces.
